resolutionContract.hashInput: fully resolved category, detail level, ordered annexes, assumptions, catalog version, maturity, and resolution contract version
resolutionContract.hashOutput: resolved template manifest sha256 and discovery-index entry
rules: Resolve one exact category id@version before applying a detail level.
Apply annexes only in the operator-declared order; every required annex must already be present.
Validate the annex requires graph with depth-first traversal; reject any back-edge as a dependency cycle before resolution.
Reject duplicate, unknown, incompatible, cyclic, floating-version, or hash-drift inputs.
Append unique category, level, and annex decisions, requirements, and verifications; never overwrite earlier entries silently.
User answers may resolve declared decisions and supply repository facts but may not delete source-derived requirements.
Any incompatible assumption or unresolved consequential decision returns HOLD or FAIL rather than a default.

requiredLineage: ordered annex ids, versions, and sha256 values
exportContract.failurePolicy: Fail closed when deterministic validation, lineage, target repository, archetype, area, or live parser validation is unavailable.

assumptionVocabulary.description: The product intentionally has no identity, account, session, role, or resource-ownership model.
Every required workflow must complete without network access or a remotely hosted dependency.
The primary workflow requires an active network connection and does not promise offline completion.

executionModeDefinitions.direct: One bounded builder owns implementation and integration; no parallel workstreams are implied.
executionModeDefinitions.swarm: Multiple dependency-aware workstreams execute under explicit ownership, integration, and approval gates.
executionModeDefinitions.undecided: Execution topology is a blocking human decision; the artifact remains HOLD and cannot be exported for factory execution until resolved.

detailLevels.description: A bounded, testable first release for one primary user journey.
additionalDecisions: What is the smallest usable vertical slice?
What must explicitly remain out of scope?

detailLevels.description: A product-quality build with persistent state, lifecycle behavior, and operational verification.
additionalDecisions: Which data and lifecycle contracts are authoritative?
Which failure and recovery behavior is required?

detailLevels.description: A multi-phase or consequential build with provenance, contracts, ownership, rollout, and evidence gates.
additionalDecisions: Which repository and branch policy are authoritative?
Who may approve promotion, merge, migration, deployment, and publication?
What rollback restores code, data, and external side effects?

annexes.description: Identity, session, authorization, ownership, and account lifecycle controls.
decisions: Which identity provider and session model are authoritative?
Which roles and resource-ownership rules apply?
requirements: Enforce authorization server-side for every protected resource.
Define sign-in, sign-out, session expiry, and account recovery behavior.
verifications: Exercise allowed and denied role-resource combinations.
Prove secrets and privileged decisions are absent from the client bundle.

annexes.description: Availability, reservation conflicts, cancellation, and time-zone behavior.
decisions: What defines canonical availability and conflict resolution?
Which cancellation and time-zone policies apply?
requirements: Prevent overlapping confirmed reservations.
Represent availability and booking timestamps with explicit time-zone semantics.
verifications: Run concurrent booking conflict scenarios.
Test daylight-saving and cross-time-zone boundaries.

annexes.description: Payment intent, settlement, refund, webhook, and reconciliation behavior.
decisions: Which provider, currency, fee, refund, and tax policies apply?
Which event is authoritative for fulfillment?
requirements: Process payment side effects idempotently.
Reconcile provider events with local order state and retain failure evidence.
verifications: Replay duplicate and out-of-order webhook events.
Exercise failed, canceled, refunded, and partially completed payments.

annexes.description: Upload, storage, transformation, moderation, accessibility, and retention of media.
decisions: Which formats, size limits, storage provider, and retention rules apply?
Which moderation and alt-text requirements apply?
requirements: Validate media type and size server-side before durable storage.
Provide accessible alternatives and deterministic failure states.
verifications: Exercise valid, oversized, malformed, and unsupported uploads.
Verify transformed assets retain ownership and accessibility metadata.

annexes.description: Offline operation, local persistence, synchronization, and conflict handling.
decisions: Which workflows must work offline?
Which conflict-resolution and data-loss policies apply?
requirements: Retain committed offline work across restart.
Surface synchronization conflicts without silently discarding user data.
verifications: Run create-edit-delete flows without network connectivity.
Reconnect with conflicting server and client changes.

annexes.description: Live state propagation, presence, ordering, reconnect, and stale-state handling.
decisions: Which events require realtime delivery and ordering?
What reconnect and stale-state policy applies?
requirements: Preserve event ordering and authorization across reconnects.
Expose stale or disconnected state to the user.
verifications: Exercise reconnect, duplicate, reordered, and unauthorized events.
Measure propagation latency against the declared budget.

annexes.description: Model contracts, evaluation sets, fallbacks, uncertainty, and human escalation.
decisions: Which model capability and provider contracts are required?
Which evaluation thresholds and escalation conditions govern release?
requirements: Evaluate production-equivalent model and retrieval paths on versioned fixtures.
Expose uncertainty and route defined failures without fabricating success.
verifications: Run deterministic schema checks and versioned quality evaluations.
Exercise provider failure, timeout, refusal, and degraded-output paths.

annexes.description: Schema or data migration, compatibility windows, rollback, and reconciliation.
decisions: What are the source and target schemas and compatibility window?
What data rollback or forward-repair strategy applies?
requirements: Preserve declared data invariants throughout migration.
Provide bounded retry, reconciliation, and an operator-visible stop condition.
verifications: Run migration against representative and malformed fixtures.
Prove rollback or forward repair on a partially applied migration.

annexes.description: Coordinate, unit, timestep, determinism, coupled-model, and numerical-tolerance contracts.
decisions: Which coordinate systems, units, timestep, and seed are canonical?
Which reference model and numerical tolerances establish correctness?
requirements: Use one canonical parameter definition across coupled simulation consumers.
Separate deterministic state validation from tolerance-based rendering and target-hardware evidence.
verifications: Run seeded state-replay and numerical reference fixtures.
Measure coupled CPU, GPU, or service-model parity within declared tolerance.

annexes.description: Device capabilities, permissions, performance, compatibility, and target-hardware evidence.
decisions: Which devices, operating systems, drivers, and peripherals are supported?
Which target-hardware performance thresholds apply?
requirements: Detect unsupported hardware and permission states explicitly.
Separate simulated checks from target-hardware certification.
verifications: Run the compatibility matrix on declared targets.
Retain target-hardware measurements with environment metadata.

annexes.description: Domain-specific legal, safety, privacy, audit, and human-approval controls.
decisions: Which jurisdiction, policy, risk classification, and qualified approver apply?
Which records and decisions require immutable audit evidence?
requirements: Fail closed when required policy or qualified approval is unavailable.
Retain auditable provenance for consequential data and decisions.
verifications: Map every control to authoritative policy and evidence.
Run misuse, unauthorized-access, retention, and audit-retrieval scenarios.

annexes.description: Health, logs, metrics, traces, alerts, and operator recovery evidence.
decisions: Which service objectives and alerts are actionable?
Which telemetry is safe to retain and for how long?
requirements: Expose health and failure states without leaking secrets or sensitive payloads.
Connect actionable alerts to an owner and recovery procedure.
verifications: Inject representative failures and verify telemetry and alert routing.
Audit logs for credential and sensitive-data leakage.

categories.definition: Browser-delivered products centered on pages, forms, workflows, and responsive interaction.
categories.counterexample: A headless payment API whose primary contract is machine-to-machine.
nonGoals: Do not require a backend when local persistence satisfies the product.
Do not infer authentication or payments from visual similarity alone.
requiredDecisions: Which user journey is primary?
Which browsers and responsive breakpoints are supported?
What persistence and authentication, if any, are required?
requirements: Render every primary workflow with loading, empty, error, and populated states.
Support keyboard navigation and declared accessibility targets.
Preserve user-visible state across the declared persistence boundary.
verifications: Run browser flows for the primary journey.
Capture desktop and mobile evidence.
Run accessibility and static checks.

categories.definition: Hosted multi-user products with accounts, roles, persistent organizational data, and service lifecycle behavior.
categories.counterexample: A single-user local tool with no accounts, shared data, or hosted service.
nonGoals: Do not add multi-tenancy to a single-user prototype.
Do not treat client-side role checks as authorization.
requiredDecisions: What is the tenant boundary?
Which roles and ownership rules apply?
Which subscription and account lifecycle states exist?
requirements: Isolate tenant data on every server-side access path.
Enforce role and ownership permissions for each protected action.
Represent trial, active, past-due, canceled, and recovery states when billing is in scope.
verifications: Run cross-tenant denial tests.
Exercise role and lifecycle transition matrices.
Reconcile billing and account state where applicable.

categories.definition: Phone or tablet products constrained by platform permissions, device lifecycle, connectivity, and distribution.
categories.counterexample: A responsive website with no native device capability or app-store distribution.
nonGoals: Do not claim cross-platform parity without device evidence.
Do not request permissions before the user reaches the relevant workflow.
requiredDecisions: Which platforms and minimum OS versions are supported?
Which device permissions are necessary?
What offline and background behavior is required?
requirements: Handle permission granted, denied, restricted, and revoked states.
Preserve committed work across backgrounding and process restart.
Meet declared platform packaging and distribution requirements.
verifications: Run the supported device and OS matrix.
Exercise permission and lifecycle transitions.
Verify offline and reconnect behavior where declared.

categories.definition: Installed workstation products using local files, operating-system integration, packaging, and upgrade behavior.
categories.counterexample: A browser-only dashboard with no local filesystem or desktop distribution needs.
nonGoals: Do not overwrite user files without recoverable backups.
Do not promise OS support that is not exercised.
requiredDecisions: Which operating systems and architectures are supported?
Which filesystem locations and file formats are authoritative?
How are upgrades, rollback, and data recovery handled?
requirements: Use atomic or recoverable writes for user-owned files.
Handle missing, locked, malformed, and externally modified files.
Package and update the application on declared operating systems.
verifications: Run filesystem failure and recovery fixtures.
Test packaging and upgrade on each declared OS.
Verify data remains readable across supported versions.

categories.definition: Interactive entertainment products governed by a game loop, controls, rules, feedback, content, and performance.
categories.counterexample: A scientific physics sandbox whose primary purpose is measurement rather than play.
nonGoals: Do not use screenshots as the only evidence for motion or feel.
Do not expand content before the core loop is playable and verified.
requiredDecisions: What is the repeatable core loop and win or loss condition?
Which controls, platforms, and target hardware apply?
Which art, audio, physics, and performance qualities are protected?
requirements: Maintain deterministic game-state transitions under a declared seed where feasible.
Provide responsive controls and explicit pause, restart, focus-loss, and input-device behavior.
Meet the declared frame-time budget in a repeatable stress scenario.
verifications: Replay canonical input and state scenarios.
Capture time-separated visual or video evidence.
Measure frame times and dropped frames on the target tier.

categories.definition: Spatial or numerical systems whose correctness depends on coordinate, time, physics, rendering, and model parity.
categories.counterexample: A stylized 2D game with no model-fidelity or spatial-analysis requirement.
nonGoals: Do not claim physical fidelity without a reference model and tolerance.
Do not require pixel-identical rendering across different GPUs.
requiredDecisions: Which coordinate systems, units, and time model are canonical?
Which physical or visual reference establishes correctness?
Which hardware and tolerance budgets apply?
requirements: Use one canonical definition for shared simulation parameters.
Keep coupled CPU and GPU calculations within declared tolerance.
Separate deterministic state validation from tolerant visual comparison.
verifications: Compare numerical results against canonical fixtures.
Run parity tests across coupled implementations.
Capture temporal, visual, and target-hardware performance evidence.

categories.definition: Machine-facing services governed by endpoint, schema, authorization, error, reliability, and compatibility contracts.
categories.counterexample: A static portfolio whose primary behavior is rendered content.
nonGoals: Do not expose internal exceptions as public API contracts.
Do not infer idempotency or compatibility behavior.
requiredDecisions: Which protocol, schema, and compatibility policy are authoritative?
Which callers and authorization rules apply?
Which latency, throughput, and availability budgets apply?
requirements: Validate inputs and authorization before side effects.
Return stable machine-readable error contracts.
Preserve declared backward compatibility or version explicitly.
verifications: Run schema and consumer contract tests.
Exercise authentication, authorization, malformed input, and idempotency.
Measure load and recovery against declared budgets.

categories.definition: Products whose user-visible behavior materially depends on model inference, retrieval, classification, or generation.
categories.counterexample: A deterministic rules engine that does not use model inference.
nonGoals: Do not use model opinion as deterministic validation.
Do not publish benchmark results from a path unavailable to production.
requiredDecisions: Which model capability, provider, data, and latency contracts apply?
Which evaluation set and thresholds govern release?
Which failures require fallback, refusal, or human review?
requirements: Version prompts, models, retrieval behavior, and evaluation fixtures.
Expose uncertainty and defined refusal or escalation behavior.
Keep evaluation and production execution paths equivalent.
verifications: Run deterministic output-schema and safety checks.
Evaluate quality on a versioned representative cohort.
Exercise provider outage, timeout, refusal, and degraded-output paths.

categories.definition: Pipelines, analytical products, and decision surfaces governed by schema, lineage, freshness, quality, and reproducibility.
categories.counterexample: A content website with no analytical or data-processing contract.
nonGoals: Do not silently coerce malformed records.
Do not display metrics without source, timestamp, and definition.
requiredDecisions: Which source systems and schemas are authoritative?
Which freshness, completeness, and quality thresholds apply?
How are backfills, late data, retention, and recovery handled?
requirements: Validate data at each declared boundary.
Record lineage, transformation version, and freshness metadata.
Make backfill and partial-failure behavior idempotent and observable.
verifications: Run representative, missing, duplicate, late, and malformed data fixtures.
Reproduce published metrics from versioned inputs.
Exercise partial failure, retry, and backfill.

categories.definition: Triggered workflows that perform repeatable actions, often with external side effects and unattended failure modes.
categories.counterexample: An interactive dashboard that never performs scheduled or event-driven actions.
nonGoals: Do not retry irreversible actions without an idempotency contract.
Do not treat silence as successful completion.
requiredDecisions: Which trigger, cadence, time zone, and concurrency rules apply?
Which side effects require approval?
Which failures retry, alert, pause, or require reconciliation?
requirements: Make each repeatable side effect idempotent or explicitly non-retriable.
Record trigger, attempt, outcome, and reconciliation identity.
Report material failure through an owned channel.
verifications: Replay duplicate and overlapping triggers.
Inject transient and permanent failures.
Verify success, partial success, retry, and escalation records.

categories.definition: Connections between independently governed systems with authentication, mapping, rate, consistency, and reconciliation boundaries.
categories.counterexample: An internal function call within one codebase and one transaction boundary.
nonGoals: Do not assume remote identifiers or enum values are stable.
Do not expose integration credentials to clients or logs.
requiredDecisions: Which system is authoritative for each field and lifecycle state?
Which authentication and credential-rotation model applies?
How are rate limits, duplicates, drift, and reconciliation handled?
requirements: Version field and enum mappings.
Handle rate limits, pagination, retries, and idempotency explicitly.
Detect and reconcile divergence without silently overwriting authoritative state.
verifications: Run mapping and contract fixtures against authoritative schemas.
Exercise pagination, rate limit, duplicate, deletion, and drift scenarios.
Verify credential redaction and rotation behavior.

categories.definition: Tools consumed by developers through commands, configuration, generated artifacts, editor behavior, or machine-readable output.
categories.counterexample: A consumer application with no developer-facing contract.
nonGoals: Do not return exit zero after a failed requested operation.
Do not mutate user projects without a dry run or explicit command.
requiredDecisions: Which commands, inputs, outputs, and exit codes are stable?
Which runtimes, versions, and project layouts are supported?
Which mutations require dry-run or confirmation?
requirements: Document stable command and machine-output contracts.
Return nonzero status for failed requested operations.
Preserve user-authored content and provide deterministic fixtures.
verifications: Run help, valid, invalid, and failure command fixtures.
Test supported runtime and configuration matrices.
Compare generated artifacts deterministically.

categories.definition: Runtime, deployment, monitoring, backup, and platform capabilities whose failures affect other systems.
categories.counterexample: A static local document with no runtime or operational dependency.
nonGoals: Do not equate a passing health check with a live consumer.
Do not provision persistent cost without an identified caller or trigger.
requiredDecisions: Which environments, consumers, identities, and network boundaries apply?
Which service objectives, rollback, backup, and recovery targets apply?
Who owns incidents and destructive changes?
requirements: Identify the concrete production caller, trigger, or consumer.
Use least-privilege identities and explicit secret boundaries.
Provide health, rollback, backup, and recovery evidence.
verifications: Run transport, health, failure-injection, and recovery tests.
Prove reachability from the named production consumer.
Exercise backup restoration and rollback without relying on the failed system.

categories.definition: Brownfield features, fixes, migrations, refactors, and remediations constrained by existing behavior and repository contracts.
categories.counterexample: A greenfield product with no existing code, data, users, or compatibility obligations.
nonGoals: Do not redesign unrelated modules during a bounded change.
Do not delete or rename without sweeping live references.
requiredDecisions: Which current behavior and interfaces are protected?
Which files, schemas, callers, and deployments are affected?
Which rollout, compatibility, data, and rollback constraints apply?
requirements: Reproduce or document the current behavior before editing.
Preserve protected capabilities and unrelated user changes.
Verify callers, migrations, configuration, and runtime paths after the change.
verifications: Run focused regression and protected-behavior tests.
Trace affected callers and configuration references.
Exercise rollout and rollback or forward-repair paths.
